newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says not guaranteeing Bakun dam.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says not guaranteeing Bakun dam.

text.p: The Malaysian government denied press reports on Thursday that it would provide a financial guarantee for the controversial $5.5 billion-Bakun dam project in the eastern state of Sarawak.
"The Malaysian government has always been supportive of the Bakun dam project. It is considered a national project," said Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie.
"We have agreed to provide a letter of comfort to the banks involved in the bridging finance to the contractors pending the (Bakun stock) listing."
But, he added, "It is not a guarantee. The Malaysian government is not in the habit of providing guarantees to the private sector."
"After the stock exchange listing, the letter of comfort then lapses," Moggie added. He was speaking to reporters at a signing ceremony between Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp (BHEC) and its shareholders.

The Bakun dam, being constructed in the rainforests of Sarawak state on Borneo island, is expected to be completed by 2003. The stock listing of BHEC, the holding company for the dam, is expected to be done in June this year.
The issue, consisting of 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit (80 U.S. cents) each, would be the single largest flotation on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange to date.
Ting Pek Khiing, executive chairman of Ekran Bhd, which is the main contractor of the project, confirmed that 10 percent of BHEC would be offered to foreign and local institutional investors.

Previously, Ekran had said 10 percent of BHEC would be offered to foreigners. Talk emerged last week that the portion for foreign investors would be scrapped because of the lukewarm response. But the adviser for the initial public offering (IPO) denied such speculation last week.

Questioned by reporters on Thursday, Ting said the 10 percent was also opened up to Malaysian institutions because of interest from that segment. But he said that the shares would be on a "first come, first served basis".
On Thursday, the Financial Times quoted one of Bakun's lead contractors, ABB Asea Brown Boveri, as saying Malaysia had agreed to guarantee financing of the project.
The newspaper quoted ABB chief executive Goran Lindahl, who spoke on Wednesday after meetings with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and his Cabinet.

At the ceremony on Thursday, Ekran, Sarawak state investment arm, Sarawak Electricity Supply Corporation, Tenaga Nasional Bhd and the government's investment arm, Khazanah Nasional Bhd, signed the shareholders agreement giving them a total of 75 percent of the holdings of Bakun Hydro-Electric.
The construction of a tunnel diverting a river prior to the building of the main dam had been delayed, but only by around two-and-a-half months, Ekran's Ting said at the news conference.
"As long as the tunnel is completed by the wet season in 1998, we are still very much in time for the construction of the dam," said Moggie.
